steps.name: Verify delivered DE table and sample structure
caveats: This step does not perform blind vst/PCA because no new model is fitted on the delivered counts; the sample-structure check is limited to library sizes, detected genes, and the metadata — and is reported as inherited where the counts cannot support it
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-eight-arms-with-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon, 12000 x 13, first column gene symbol), /eval-eight-arms-with-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 samples, condition), and /eval-eight-arms-with-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (DESeq2 treated-vs-control results, 12000 x 8). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. No model is fitted in this step — the DE test was already run and its results are taken as delivered.

Do not refit differential expression; verify the delivered table only (R-0110@41cb)
State the input contrast, its reference level, and the log2FC sign convention in the step output
acceptance_criteria: DE table parsed: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, stat, p-value and adjusted p-value columns identified and typed
Contrast direction stated: which level is numerator vs denominator, and the sign convention of log2FC/stat, taken from the table and metadata (enrichment direction depends on it)
Count matrix row/column counts reconciled against the DE table (12000 genes, 13 samples minus any ID column); gene-symbol identifier space confirmed shared between counts and DE table
Library size and detected-gene count reported per sample; sample_01's low depth quantified and kept (no silent removal — R-0008@440d)
Counts of NA p-values and NA adjusted p-values in the DE table reported and attributed (independent filtering vs Cook's-distance outlier flags)
Significant-gene count at padj < 0.05 reported; if below ~50, ORA is recorded as unpowered and the ranked method is the sole enrichment path (R-0103@93aa)

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on Wald statistic vs MSigDB Hallmark
caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent; this single-method result is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding (R-0055@107a)
Gene length and expression bias affect over-representation tests; the ranked full-list design and tested-genes universe mitigate rather than remove this
steps.context: Rank metric choice: the Wald statistic is signed and scaled by its standard error, so low-count noise does not dominate the top of the list; ranking by the unshrunken log2FC alone or by signed -log10 p-values (which saturate and tie) is explicitly rejected. The ranked method is used on the full list because hallmark signal in AD skin is often coordinated small shifts rather than individually significant genes; an over-representation test would only be run if the significant list were large, and the T1S1 count governs that. GMT is a local staged reference — no download.

min_size = 15, max_size = 500 after intersecting each set with the tested genes; window reported (R-0047@fd9d)

Universe = the tested genes of the delivered DE table; stated in output (R-0046@a0ac, R-0054@801e)

acceptance_criteria: Full ranked list built from ALL tested genes in the DE table (no padj or LFC pre-cut), ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column); tie rule stated (stable order on ties, no randomization)
Gene symbols carried as-is: the DE table and the hallmark GMT are both HGNC-symbol space, so no identifier mapping is applied; the share of tested genes that match no GMT symbol reported

Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the tested hallmark sets; significant sets reported at q < 0.05 with ES, NES, and the positive/negative direction stated relative to the treated level
Leading-edge genes extracted per significant set and written beside their stat values
Permutation seed recorded in the output

caveats: If the hallmark pass yields few or no significant sets, this step still runs and its null/weak result is reported as the corroboration picture rather than skipped
steps.context: The hallmark collection condenses founder signatures but does not name mechanisms; a curated second collection resolves a broad hit (e.g. inflammatory cytokine signaling) to a specific annotated pathway. plan.title: Hallmark enrichment from delivered AD DE results
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset already carries a DESeq2 results table for the atopic dermatitis lesional (treated) vs control contrast, and the research question asks only which hallmark pathways are enriched — so no new differential expression test is fitted; the plan starts from the delivered table. The DE table is verified first (contrast direction, reference level, sign convention, NA pattern, and the sample_01 low-depth caveat reported against the delivered counts), because every enrichment direction depends on the sign convention of the input contrast. Genes are then ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) — the signed, uncertainty-scaled metric chosen over the unshrunken log2FC (noisy at low counts) and over signed -log10 p-values (ties at saturation) — and the full ranked list of all tested genes is run through a preranked GSEA (gseapy, Python per user constraint) against the MSigDB Hallmark collection (50 sets, human, 2026.1, HGNC symbols), with gene sets windowed to 15-500 members and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the 50 sets. A second pass against the WikiPathways human collection (2026.07.10 release) resolves broad hallmark hits to named pathways; the two collections are never merged and each is reported with its release. The report lists leading-edge genes per significant set, collapses redundant sets, and carries the reproducibility record (database, version, rank metric, universe, size window, seed). All scripts are Python: pandas for the table work and gseapy for prerank GSEA; no R.
